patterns.what_worked: Read the reference repo per branch with `git show <branch>:<path>` and `git grep <branch>` instead of guessing from the checked-out branch: that is what turned 'the re-audit's L-3 premise' into a REFUTATION (SpellBookDocumentation.lua:82 on classic_era DOES carry Name = "IsSpellKnown", and loadDeprecationFallbacks is in 33 files there, 40 on live). Each API was then answered with branch:file:line + a quote, and the load-game-type gating on origin/forever (camelot vs mainline) was checked too, which surfaced two facts no one had: the UnitAura global is classic-gated (absent on Retail and on the WoW Forever client) and the totem slot constants are not defined as globals on WoW Forever.
patterns.what_was_hard: The checklist's framing invited false premises: check 7 asserted '0 hits on classic_era' for IsSpellKnownOrInSpellBook (there is one, at :98), check 13's '0 call sites on classic_era' had to be separated from 'the C API does not exist' (it is absent from the TREE on all five branches - a native global with no FrameXML call site and no doc entry), and check 14's '3rd return' does not exist - GetSpellPowerCost has ONE return (an array of SpellPowerCostInfo), and the addon's consumers read costs[1].cost (warrior/druid) or the type-matched entry (rogue), not index 3. Answering those honestly rather than in the checklist's terms took the cross-checking.
patterns.skill_gap: Reading a native C API's contract out of a FrameXML tree is impossible when Blizzard's own code no longer calls it (the classic global GetItemInfo): the tree can only say 'absent from the tree'. That limit had to be stated in the truth table instead of papered over with a remembered shape.
